proposed_comments.title: Refresh command-bar state when the selected item is reused
proposed_comments.body:
### Refresh command-bar state when the selected item is reused

**Severity:** `medium`

When the selected item reference is unchanged, this setter returns before recalculating the primary, secondary, and overflow command state. A repeated selection can therefore leave the command bar showing stale actions after the underlying command snapshot changes. Refresh the derived context items before returning from the same-reference path.

```suggestion
                UpdateContextItems();
                return;
```

confidence.rationale: The early return is directly on the changed selected-item setter path; reselecting the same object after its command snapshot changes leaves command-bar actions stale unless the derived state is refreshed.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve context-item compatibility (1/2)
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve context-item compatibility (1/2)

**Severity:** `medium`

This PR replaces the old MoreCommands backing concept with the unified context-item snapshot, but existing derived/partial code can still depend on the previous unsafe alias. Keeping the alias pointed at the same backing list preserves source compatibility without changing runtime behavior. Apply this together with the companion namespace import.

```suggestion
    protected List<IContextItemViewModel> UnsafeContextItems => _contextItems;

    protected List<IContextItemViewModel> UnsafeMoreCommands => _contextItems;
```
proposed_comments.suggestion:
protected List<IContextItemViewModel> UnsafeContextItems => _contextItems;

    protected List<IContextItemViewModel> UnsafeMoreCommands => _contextItems;

confidence.rationale: The compatibility alias is a source-level preservation fix for existing partial/subclass code that still refers to the old MoreCommands backing member while sharing the same underlying context item list.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve context-item compatibility (2/2)
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve context-item compatibility (2/2)

**Severity:** `medium`

The snapshot type is in the `Models` namespace while its constructor and properties use view-model types from the parent namespace. Add the explicit import so the compatibility-preserving snapshot model compiles consistently with the alias change. Apply this together with the companion alias suggestion.

```suggestion
using Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels;

namespace Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.Models;
```

confidence.rationale: The snapshot model declares view-model typed properties from a nested Models namespace; the explicit import is required for the exact patched tree to compile consistently.

proposed_comments.title: Anchor the hidden-More flyout to a visible command button
proposed_comments.body:
### Anchor the hidden-More flyout to a visible command button

**Severity:** `medium`

When the More button is hidden, Ctrl+K still opens the context menu, but the current fallback anchors the flyout to the whole command bar. That can place the menu away from the active command controls and makes focus restoration less predictable. Pick the visible More, secondary, or primary button as the anchor instead.

```suggestion
                    var target = ViewModel.ShouldShowMoreCommandsButton ?
                        MoreCommandsButton :
                        ViewModel.HasSecondaryCommand ? SecondaryButton : PrimaryButton;

                    ContextMenuFlyout.ShowAt(
                        target,
```
proposed_comments.suggestion:
var target = ViewModel.ShouldShowMoreCommandsButton ?
                        MoreCommandsButton :
                        ViewModel.HasSecondaryCommand ? SecondaryButton : PrimaryButton;

                    ContextMenuFlyout.ShowAt(
                        target,

confidence.rationale: The current fallback anchors the flyout to the whole command bar when the More button is hidden; choosing a visible command button keeps placement and focus behavior localized to the actual command surface.

proposed_comments.title: Prevent duplicate shortcut execution (1/6)
proposed_comments.body:
### Prevent duplicate shortcut execution (1/6)

**Severity:** `high`

Primary shortcuts can be handled by both the command bar and the embedded context menu after the flyout control has been created, causing a command to execute twice. Track the flyout close event so the context menu only participates in global shortcut dispatch while it is actually open. Apply all suggestions in this group together.

```suggestion
                x:Name="ContextMenuFlyout"
                Closed="ContextMenuFlyout_Closed"
```

confidence.rationale: Both the command bar and embedded context menu receive the same global shortcut message; tracking flyout close state is required for the exact single-consumer fix.

proposed_comments.title: Prevent duplicate shortcut execution (2/6)

confidence.rationale: The receiver currently processes the message even if another receiver already handled it and even while the flyout is open; either condition can duplicate command execution.

proposed_comments.title: Prevent duplicate shortcut execution (3/6)
proposed_comments.body:
### Prevent duplicate shortcut execution (3/6)

**Severity:** `high`

Set the embedded context menu's open-state flag when the flyout opens. This lets shortcut dispatch switch to the flyout while it is active instead of allowing both controls to handle the same command. Apply all suggestions in this group together.

```suggestion
        ContextControl.IsFlyoutOpen = true;

        // Focus the filter box so the flyout captures keyboard input,
```
proposed_comments.suggestion:
ContextControl.IsFlyoutOpen = true;

        // Focus the filter box so the flyout captures keyboard input,

confidence.rationale: The embedded context menu needs an explicit open-state flag before it can safely decide whether to consume global shortcut messages.

proposed_comments.title: Prevent duplicate shortcut execution (4/6)

confidence.rationale: The open-state flag must be cleared on flyout close so global shortcuts return to command-bar handling after the menu is dismissed.

proposed_comments.title: Prevent duplicate shortcut execution (5/6)
proposed_comments.body:
### Prevent duplicate shortcut execution (5/6)

**Severity:** `high`

The context menu is registered for shortcut messages as soon as the control is instantiated, which is earlier than the flyout being open. Add an internal open-state flag so the receiver can ignore global shortcut messages while closed. Apply all suggestions in this group together.

```suggestion
    public ContextMenuViewModel ViewModel { get; }

    internal bool IsFlyoutOpen { get; set; }
```
proposed_comments.suggestion:
public ContextMenuViewModel ViewModel { get; }

    internal bool IsFlyoutOpen { get; set; }

confidence.rationale: The control needs an internal state bit to distinguish instantiated-but-closed from actively open; relying on registration alone caused the duplicate handling.

proposed_comments.title: Prevent duplicate shortcut execution (6/6)

confidence.rationale: The current receiver invokes commands without checking whether the flyout is open or whether another receiver already handled the message; this is the direct duplicate-execution path.

proposed_comments.title: Assert separators do not create overflow actions
proposed_comments.body:
### Assert separators do not create overflow actions

**Severity:** `low`

This test verifies that leading separators do not block secondary-command selection, but it does not assert the related More-button invariant. Add the overflow assertion so a future regression cannot show the More button for a single visible secondary command just because separators are present.

```suggestion
        Assert.AreEqual("Secondary", viewModel.SecondaryCommand.Name);
        Assert.IsFalse(viewModel.HasOverflowCommands);
```

confidence.rationale: The test already constructs the separator-plus-secondary case; the added assertion captures the specific no-overflow invariant this PR is intended to preserve.

proposed_comments.title: Assert content-page updates keep the More button hidden
proposed_comments.body:
### Assert content-page updates keep the More button hidden

**Severity:** `low`

The content-page update path already verifies the refreshed primary and secondary commands, but it should also preserve the no-overflow state when only those visible actions remain. Add the assertion so content-page command refreshes cannot regress the hidden-More behavior.

```suggestion
        Assert.AreEqual("Updated Secondary", viewModel.SecondaryCommandName);
        Assert.IsFalse(viewModel.HasOverflowCommands);
```

confidence.rationale: The existing content-page update test already checks the derived primary/secondary state after command replacement; adding the overflow assertion protects the same UI invariant for content pages.
